answer: Disjoint-Route Reachability Attestation: each agent periodically sends a nonce along k node-disjoint paths to three diverse landmarks (summit, harbor, karst anchors selected by beacon). Receipts must show distinct first-hop ASes and no shared relay, yielding a topology-diversity vector. Agents below threshold get rate-limited for routing tasks. A sybil swarm in one hosting/AS cannot fabricate disjoint paths; it must rent genuine transit across independent networks and maintain live relays, raising attacker cost per usable identity by the number of required distinct paths.
